questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Australia because I had heard great things about the country and the opportunities it offered for outdoor activities and exploration. Additionally, Australia provided excellent travel opportunities after my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I chose Melbourne, but looking back, I think I would have preferred Sydney – it’s such a great city

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a very long process, and you need to be prepared for the many official documents and applications you have to keep track of. However, I found that there was good communication from both KU and Melbourne University if I needed any help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have an office called Stop-One that can help you with anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There are plenty of student accommodations in Melbourne, but they are very expensive. I ended up renting an Airbnb with a friend near campus – it was cheaper, though a bit more basic compared to the pricier student housing options.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of student accommodations in Melbourne, but they are very expensive. I ended up renting an Airbnb with a friend near campus – it was cheaper, though a bit more basic compared to the pricier student housing options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find accommodation close to campus so you can participate in social activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great student housing but too expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They held an online meeting where all students were informed about practical matters such as visa, course registration, health insurance, etc. Additionally, you can always contact their student support service, Stop-One, but it can take some time for them to respond, especially when things are busy just before the start of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always contact them but it can take a while for them to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registered for most of the classes from home, but I had some issues with the portal. I was only fully registered when I arrived there and received help from Stop-One.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to start early and participate in the online meetings. This will help you stay informed and prepared for the registration process.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at my host institution was quite similar to that at UCPH in terms of the structure of classes with lectures and tutorials. However, a notable difference was that most lectures were recorded, allowing students to watch them remotely if they preferred. Also, they held a lot of midterm exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Microbes, Infections and Responses
Australia in the Wine World
Our Planet, Our Health
Medical Microbiology: Virology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses I would recommend depend on your interests, but if you're looking for something enjoyable, I would suggest taking the wine course. It's a fun subject where you learn about wine production, wine regions, and get to participate in various wine tastings.

questions.answer: Medical bills and medication also turned out to be costly, even though I had the mandatory health insurance.

questions.answer: Food was quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the non-academic opportunities at my host institution. There were many engaged students and a wide range of clubs to join, including hiking, surfing, swimming, and all kinds of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend renting a car with some friends and going on a road trip along the Great Ocean Road. It's incredibly beautiful and a must-see experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking as many trips as possible, visiting wildlife sanctuaries, or joining some of the excursions offered by the social clubs, such as hiking, surfing, or diving trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: t was quite easy to adjust, as I spent most of my time with other exchange students. Their society and culture are similar to our own.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, I didn’t socialize much with local students. It seemed like the majority of students were international, and I’m not sure where the Australians were.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I had hoped to experience more of the Australian culture, but Melbourne is very international and strongly influenced by students from Asian countries.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The part of the culture I appreciated the most was what I experienced during my travels along the east coast after my studies. Australians are very laid-back and friendly, they have a chill vibe. I also love their nature and all the cool activities you can do, like diving, hiking, surfing, boat trips, waterfall tours, and much more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find accommodation close to your institution.

Be prepared to participate in a lot of social activities, especially at the beginning of your stay when people are forming their friend groups.

It's great to know some people from home, so you have someone to hang out and participate in activities with in the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be honest, the most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the weekend trips and my travels along the east coast afterwards.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At KU, we have a block structure where we take 2 courses at a time and have exams at the end of each course. In Melbourne, I had 4 courses at once, each with ongoing mid-term exams that counted for a percentage of the final exam. This meant I was constantly studying for exams in one of the courses, and once that was over, I had to start studying for the next one. It was a bit of an exhausting system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Being on exchange is very rewarding but also quite challenging. Remember to apply for as many scholarships as possible well in advance. I would also recommend leaving some time afterward for travel.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
